edits.text: 1) Incomplete-predicate / standalone-assertion test: Ask whether the left chunk, read on its own, already makes a concrete factual claim (for example: a finite verb that appears complete, an ordinal or numbered/list item, or a statement of outcome) whose truth or interpretation depends on material that follows. If YES, treat the cut as very high-risk: either set cohesion near 0 or raise contra toward 1. Operational guidance: when the left fragment alone asserts a specific outcome that the continuation can modify or negate (e.g. an item of an enumeration later resolved by 'respectively', or a verb whose required complement/argument appears later), increase contra strongly (for example >= 0.8) or set cohesion very low. This rule overrides small-surface preferences for short pieces; prefer to keep such assertions attached to their disambiguating material.

2) Detached-head / essential-modifier test: Ask whether the cut would separate a syntactic head (person/place name, noun-phrase head, finite verb) from an essential modifier, determiner, title element, or other attached words that determine its interpretation. If YES, sharply reduce cohesion (treat the joined-translation fidelity as very low). Operational guidance: splitting inside multiword names or titles, or between a determiner/modifier and its head, usually yields unfaithful isolated translations; prefer cuts that leave atomic names/titles or head+modifier units intact, or else score such internal cuts near the bottom.
